title: Square-zero lifting for a separable algebraic field extension
statement: Let $L/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] which is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], with no finiteness or characteristic restriction. For every commutative $k$-algebra $D$, every ideal $J\subseteq D$ with $J^2=0$, and every homomorphism of $k$-algebras $a:L\to D/J$, there is a homomorphism of $k$-algebras $b:L\to D$ with $q\circ b=a$, where $q:D\to D/J$ is the quotient map; algebras, algebra homomorphisms, ideal products and quotient maps are as in [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient].

source.place: Proposition Tag 0322 (proposition-characterize-separable-field-extensions), characteristic zero (3) and positive characteristic (1) implies (6), specialized to a separable algebraic extension; formal smoothness is Definition Tag 00TI (definition-formally-smooth).

mathlib_match.how: Read Mathlib/RingTheory/Etale/Field.lean:98-145: Algebra.FormallyEtale.of_isSeparable k L assumes only fields, their algebra structure and Algebra.IsSeparable k L, so infinite separable algebraic extensions are included. The square-zero lifting conclusion is the surjective half of Algebra.FormallyEtale.comp_bijective, Mathlib/RingTheory/Etale/Basic.lean:77-79: with the formally etale instance supplied by of_isSeparable, apply its surjectivity to a. Thus the statement is a direct specialization of that declaration and its lifting interface, with no comparison theorem between different geometric notions. Algebra.IsSeparable says each element is separable, matching the cited algebraic separability definition.
